intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that mitochondrial complex I deficiency nuclear type 7 (MC1DN7) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the NDUFV2 gene (600532) on chromosome 18p11.

paragraphs.text: Mitochondrial complex I deficiency nuclear type 7 (MC1DN7) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutation in the NDUFV2 gene, which encodes the 24-kD subunit of complex I. Affected individuals have biochemical complex I deficiency. Reported clinical features include early-onset hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with trunk hypotonia and encephalopathy or brain atrophy, and Leigh syndrome without cardiac involvement.

paragraphs.text: Cameron et al. (2015) performed whole-exome sequencing on fibroblast DNA from 1 of 2 sibs with MC1DN7 (family 1). Filtering left 190 novel nonsynonymous variants in 185 candidate genes. Both sibs were compound heterozygous for 2 mutations in the NDUFV2 gene. One was the intronic c.IVS2+1delGTAA mutation. The other was a novel 1-bp insertion (c.669_670insG) predicted to cause a frameshift (Ser224ValfsTer3). The authors then screened 10 probands with complex I deficiency from different families. In a second, consanguineous family (family 2), they found that the affected sibs were homozygous for the c.IVS2+1delGTAA mutation.

paragraphs.text: Pagniez-Mammeri et al. (2009) screened 8 patients with biochemically proven isolated complex I deficiency for mutations in 8 nuclear complex I genes, including NDUFV2. They used Surveyor nuclease digestion of 22 cDNA fragments and found molecular defects in 3 patients. They concluded that the method was a reliable way to genotype nuclear complex I deficiencies and would enhance the possibility of prenatal diagnosis.
